## HueMux v0.0.5-alpha.2 — Tapping a slider's track sets the brightness again

> **Alpha.** Built and tested in CI, not exercised on real hardware here
> beyond a single LAN deployment. This one matters if you use the UI on
> Android: the tap-to-set behaviour of every brightness slider was broken on
> Chrome and in the app, while working normally in Firefox and on the desktop.

### What was wrong

Tapping a brightness slider's track — not its thumb — is supposed to jump the
value to the point you tapped. On Chromium it did nothing at all.

The culprit is `shared/slider-touch.js`, added because a slider spans the whole
width of a light card and therefore catches swipes meant for the page: with a
finger down on a slider, the native control jumped its thumb to wherever the
finger landed and reported a brightness change, so a scroll also changed a
light. The file withheld every `input` event from the page until the finger had
travelled at least 8px sideways, and put the value back in the meantime.

Chromium fires that first `input` on touch-down, and for a tap it is the only
one there will ever be. Withholding it withheld the tap: the value was taken
back on release and the page was never told anything. Gecko reports the change
differently, which is why Firefox on Android kept working, and a mouse never
went through this path at all.

### What it does now

The value the control chose is remembered, and if the gesture ends without the
finger having travelled, it is delivered to the page as a single `input`
event — the same event, with the same value, that the other engines send for
the same tap. Nothing is invented or recomputed from the touch coordinates; the
engine's own mapping of tap position to value is what gets committed.

The three outcomes are now:

- **Tap** — the value goes to the tapped point, one event, brightness written.
- **Drag** — past 8px sideways the page sees values live, as before.
- **Swipe** — past 8px vertically the value goes back and the page is never
  told, so no brightness write and no light change from a scroll.

A tap that lands on the thumb where it already sits is still a no-op, and no
longer reports a change that did not happen. Mouse and pen are untouched.

The Android app carries the frontend in its bundle, so the fix needs the new
APK from this release, not the previously installed one.
